program_outcomes.statement: Strategic Thinking and Managerial Decision-Making: Apply strategic frameworks to analyse business situations, evaluate alternatives, and make informed managerial decisions in complex environments.
Analytical and Data-Driven Problem Solving: Collect, analyse, and interpret quantitative and qualitative data to diagnose business problems and recommend evidence-based solutions.
Digital and Technological Fluency: Select and apply appropriate digital tools, platforms, and technologies to achieve business objectives in an increasingly digital economy.

Ethical, Social, and Inclusive Leadership: Demonstrate ethical reasoning, social responsibility, and commitment to inclusive growth in business decisions, respecting diverse stakeholders and communities.
Communication and Presentation Skills: Communicate ideas effectively in written, oral, and digital formats across languages and platforms, adapting to diverse audiences.
Entrepreneurial and Local Business Application: Apply entrepreneurial thinking and management knowledge to create, grow, and sustain local businesses, MSMEs, cooperatives, and rural enterprises.

course_outcomes.statement: Understand the foundations of creativity and innovation in a business context.
course_outcomes.mapping_justification: Grasping the creative process and the creativity-to-innovation link equips students to frame problems before deciding (PO1:2). The Unit 1 activity redesigns a mobile app or website, giving light exposure to digital product thinking (PO3:1). Creativity is taught as the foundation of enterprise renewal, directly relevant to MSMEs and local businesses (PO6:2).

course_outcomes.statement: Present creative ideas effectively using storytelling and visual tools.
course_outcomes.mapping_justification: Presenting ideas through storytelling and visual tools is squarely a communication competence, exercised in every studio pitch (PO5:3). Visual articulation uses digital mind-mapping and presentation tools (PO3:2), and the ideas being pitched are enterprise and startup propositions (PO6:2).
course_outcomes.blooms_mapping_note: Prescribed cognitive ability is 'Develop', which is not a level in Bloom's Revised Taxonomy. Mapped to 'create' because the outcome requires producing an original pitch artefact (story + visual), not merely applying a given technique. Override here if the Board of Studies intends 'apply'.

course_outcomes.statement: Use the SCAMPER technique to develop innovative ideas and solutions.
course_outcomes.mapping_justification: SCAMPER is a structured generation-and-selection method: students produce alternatives and choose among them, which is managerial decision-making (PO1:3). Its seven prompts force systematic examination of a product across dimensions (PO2:2), applied in Unit 3 to a tech product such as an app or website (PO3:2). Team SCAMPER outputs are defended aloud (PO5:1), and the object throughout is improving a real product or service (PO6:3).

course_outcomes.statement: Apply mind mapping and creative techniques to solve real-world problems.
course_outcomes.mapping_justification: Mind mapping is taught explicitly to break complex problems into manageable parts, which is structured problem diagnosis (PO2:3), and the resulting decomposition informs what to act on first (PO1:2). Unit 2 applies it to technology startup ideas and complex tech issues (PO3:2). Collaborative mind mapping is a shared visual artefact that teams reason through together (PO5:2), and the worked example is mapping the components needed to launch a venture (PO6:3).

syllabus_outline.title: Foundations of Creativity and Innovation
syllabus_outline.description: Introduction to Creativity: definition, importance, and role in problem-solving. Creativity vs. Innovation. The Creative Process. Barriers to Creativity.
key_topics: Introduction to Creativity: Definition, importance, and role in problem-solving
Creativity vs. Innovation: How creative thinking leads to innovation in business
The Creative Process: Stages of creativity - from idea generation to implementation
Barriers to Creativity: How to overcome mental blocks and traditional thinking
syllabus_outline.hands_on_activity: Brainstorm ideas to redesign a basic mobile app or website and create a creative solution

syllabus_outline.title: Mind Mapping and Creative Thinking Techniques
syllabus_outline.description: Basics and benefits of mind mapping, mind mapping for problem solving, and collaborative mind mapping for team projects.
key_topics: Introduction to Mind Mapping: Basics of mind mapping, its benefits, and how it helps with idea generation
Mind Mapping for Problem Solving: Using mind maps to break down complex tech issues into manageable parts
Collaborative Mind Mapping: How teams can use mind mapping as a creative and collaborative tool for projects
syllabus_outline.hands_on_activity: Create a mind map for a technology startup idea, visually breaking down the components needed to launch it

syllabus_outline.title: SCAMPER Technique for Innovation
syllabus_outline.description: SCAMPER as a structured creativity tool, applied to product improvement and to real-world business or tech problems in teams.
key_topics: Introduction to SCAMPER: Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate, Rearrange
Using SCAMPER for Product Improvement: Applying SCAMPER to improve existing products or services
Team SCAMPER Exercise: Working in groups to apply SCAMPER to a real-world business or tech problem
syllabus_outline.hands_on_activity: Teams apply SCAMPER to redesign or enhance a tech product (e.g., a mobile app or website)
